summary: Separate host-agent semantic audit supports final Proposition H, including its exceptional term at most 3, the counterexample to a pure epsilon-squared bound uniform in epsilon(N), the constant-one endpoint transfer lemma, exact divisor switch and sharpness witness. The critic independently inspected Ford Theorem 2.5 and its coefficient-uniform proof and the cited Mertens input, then checked the mathematical derivations. One inherited brief error was identified: at the strict quarter-root cutoff, four-factor survivors are impossible; triples explain why the four-cell model is nonexhaustive. No mathematical repair to the accepted propositions is required. The parity-sensitive lower bound remains open, numerical effective constants and novelty remain unverified, and neither result is an established Goldbach breakthrough. This is handwritten proof plus separate agent review, with no formal or external peer verification and no measured usage.

claims.text: The final pointwise H bound, with omega_{>N^alpha}(N) at most 3 and the stated uniform lower-scale term, is supported by the inspected classical two-form sieve and the complete derivation.
The constant-one moving-endpoint transfer, exact divisor switch and stated sharpness witness are supported by direct elementary argument.
The inherited claim that four prime factors may survive the strict alpha=1/4 roughness cutoff is false; at most three can survive, and triples make the P/S four-cell model nonexhaustive.
The sufficient pointwise lower bound P-open remains unproved; neither accepted proposition establishes Goldbach or a demonstrated breakthrough on it.
Novelty of the trilinear bound and numerical effective constants are unverified; the endpoint repair has announced prior-art overlap.
